safetyDisclaimer: Stopping or changing some substances suddenly can cause serious, potentially life-threatening withdrawal effects. Do not make major changes to your substance use without speaking with a qualified healthcare professional or addiction medicine physician.
nutritionDisclaimer: This is general nutrition information and is not a medical treatment plan for substance use or withdrawal. Individual dietary needs should be evaluated by a qualified healthcare professional or registered dietitian.

categories.name: Stimulants
categories.subtitle: Includes pre-workout stimulants, amphetamines, cocaine, methylphenidate, DMAA
categories.generalEffects: Elevates central nervous system activity, heart rate, blood pressure, alertness, and metabolic output.
shortTermRisks: Acute tachycardia (racing heart) and irregular cardiac rhythms (arrhythmias)
Severe insomnia, agitation, elevated body temperature (hyperthermia)
Post-usage crash accompanied by profound mental exhaustion and mood drops
longTermRisks: Cardiovascular strain, arterial hypertension, and increased stroke risk
Dopamine receptor downregulation leading to anhedonia (inability to feel pleasure)
Psychological dependence and elevated anxiety states
signsHelpNeeded: Needing escalating doses to achieve the initial awakening or focus effect
Chest tightness, shortness of breath, or dizziness during workouts
Inability to train or function normally without chemical stimulation
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Classified under WADA S6 (Stimulants). Strictly prohibited In-Competition; certain stimulants (like ephedrine or pseudoephedrine) trigger violations above urinary thresholds.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: Stimulant cessation can result in severe fatigue and depressive episodes. An addiction medicine doctor or sports psychologist can provide safe behavioural and cardiovascular monitoring.

categories.name: Steroids
categories.subtitle: Includes anabolic androgenic steroids (testosterone, oxandrolone, nandrolone), SARMs, prohormones
categories.generalEffects: Mimics male sex hormones (androgens) to artificially stimulate muscle protein synthesis and tissue hypertrophy.
shortTermRisks: Acute hormonal imbalance, acne vulgaris, and severe mood swings ('roid rage')
Fluid retention, elevated hematocrit (thickened blood), and hypertensive spikes
Early tendon vulnerability: muscle mass gains outpace tendon collagen adaptation
longTermRisks: Complete shutdown of natural hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis
Left ventricular hypertrophy, premature cardiovascular disease, and liver toxicity (oral 17-aa compounds)
Infertility, testicular atrophy, and permanent endocrine disruption
signsHelpNeeded: Experiencing extreme depressive crashes or hormonal fatigue when pausing usage
Noticeable breast tissue enlargement (gynecomastia) or testicular pain
Severe blood pressure readings (>140/90 mmHg) at rest
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Classified under WADA S1 (Anabolic Agents). Strictly prohibited at all times (both in- and out-of-competition). Results in mandatory 4-year competitive bans.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: Never attempt unmonitored post-cycle therapies (PCT) using black-market chemicals. An endocrinologist must evaluate your pituitary recovery and lipid profiles.

categories.name: Cannabis
categories.subtitle: Includes marijuana, THC extracts, edibles, synthetic cannabinoids (K2/Spice)
categories.generalEffects: Interacts with CB1 and CB2 cannabinoid receptors, modulating sensory perception, motor coordination, and mood.
shortTermRisks: Impaired reaction time, spatial judgment, and psychomotor coordination
Acute memory impairment and heightened anxiety or paranoia in sensitive individuals
Elevated resting heart rate and airway irritation if inhaled
longTermRisks: Cannabis Use Disorder (CUD) with motivational apathy
Exacerbation of underlying psychological conditions in developing brains (<25 yrs)
Cardiovascular strain during heavy concurrent physical exertion
signsHelpNeeded: Relying on cannabis daily to sleep, eat, or manage normal emotional stress
Skipping academic, athletic, or social responsibilities to consume
Experiencing persistent irritability and sleep disturbance when attempting to abstain
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Natural and synthetic cannabinoids are prohibited In-Competition under WADA S8 (except cannabidiol / CBD isolate). Urinary threshold for THC is 150 ng/mL.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: Counsellors specializing in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and sleep hygiene can help develop natural relaxation without dependency.

categories.name: Opioids
categories.subtitle: Includes prescription painkillers (tramadol, codeine, oxycodone, morphine, fentanyl)
categories.generalEffects: Binds to mu-opioid receptors in the central nervous system to blunt physical pain and produce sedation.
shortTermRisks: Respiratory depression (slowed breathing), which can rapidly become fatal in excess doses
Drowsiness, cognitive dulling, nausea, and severe constipation
Masking critical musculoskeletal injuries, causing athletes to worsen acute tears
longTermRisks: Rapid physiological tolerance and profound neurochemical physical dependence
Hyperalgesia (paradoxical increase in sensitivity to pain over time)
Life-threatening respiratory arrest and overdose risk
signsHelpNeeded: Taking painkillers beyond the prescribed surgical recovery window
Experiencing intense nausea, chills, shaking, or panic when missing a dose
Doctor shopping or seeking unprescribed pills online or from teammates
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Narcotics are prohibited In-Competition under WADA S7. Tramadol is prohibited In-Competition starting 2024 due to high addiction and injury risks.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: CRITICAL: Abrupt opioid cessation causes distressing withdrawal, and unmanaged relapse carries lethal overdose risks. Contact an addiction medicine physician immediately.

categories.name: Sedatives
categories.subtitle: Includes benzodiazepines (alprazolam, diazepam), sleep medications (Z-drugs), barbiturates
categories.generalEffects: Enhances the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA, inducing sedation, muscle relaxation, and anxiety reduction.
shortTermRisks: Severe motor incoordination, anterograde amnesia, and slurred speech
Synergistic lethality when combined with alcohol or pain medications
Rebound insomnia and acute panic upon rapid wear-off
longTermRisks: Rapid physiological dependence within weeks of regular consumption
Cognitive slowing and blunted emotional processing
Life-threatening grand mal seizures upon abrupt unmanaged cessation
signsHelpNeeded: Inability to sleep without increasing tablet dosages
Experiencing tremors, sweating, or panic attacks when missing a nightly dose
Combining sedatives with alcoholic beverages to force sleep
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Certain sedatives are monitored or restricted, and can impair safety in precision sports (e.g., shooting, archery, motor racing).
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: CRITICAL: Never stop benzodiazepines cold turkey. Sudden cessation can cause life-threatening seizures. A physician must supervise any tapering schedule.

categories.name: Alcohol
categories.subtitle: Includes beer, spirits, wine, high-proof alcoholic preparations
categories.generalEffects: Central nervous system depressant blunting prefrontal cortex inhibition and impairing motor reflexes.
shortTermRisks: Severe dehydration, electrolyte depletion, and inhibited muscle glycogen synthesis
Impaired heat regulation during workouts and heightened risk of traumatic injuries
Supressed natural growth hormone release during nighttime recovery
longTermRisks: Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver), cirrhosis, and cardiovascular cardiomyopathy
Increased risk of multiple cancers and gastrointestinal inflammation
Alcohol Use Disorder with dangerous physiological withdrawal
signsHelpNeeded: Morning drinking, memory blackouts, or drinking to steady shaky hands
Underperforming consistently in sports or academics following weekend binges
Feeling unable to socialize or decompress without alcohol
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Alcohol was historically banned in select precision sports and remains subject to individual federation discipline and campus safety codes.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: Chronic heavy alcohol cessation can trigger delirium tremens and seizures. Medical detoxification supervision is essential for heavy daily drinkers.

categories.name: Prescription Medicine Misuse
categories.subtitle: Includes ADHD stimulants (Adderall, Ritalin), asthma inhalers in excess, thyroid hormones
categories.generalEffects: Using pharmaceutical drugs without personal medical diagnosis, or taking doses exceeding doctor guidelines.
shortTermRisks: Acute hypertensive emergencies and cardiac arrhythmias
Severe anxiety, tremors, and sleep deprivation
Severe anti-doping rule violations (ADRVs) if tested
longTermRisks: Permanent cardiovascular strain and autonomic dysregulation
Psychological dependence on medication for routine academic or athletic tasks
Masking underlying stress, learning differences, or overtraining syndrome
signsHelpNeeded: Acquiring prescription medication from peers or unlicensed online sources
Taking oral salbutamol or doubling inhaler doses instead of training legitimately
Hiding medication usage from team doctors and parents
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Prescription medications require an approved Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) supported by comprehensive clinical diagnostics prior to competition.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: Consult a sports physician to evaluate genuine medical conditions and establish legitimate, non-prohibited treatment plans.

categories.name: Unknown Substances
categories.subtitle: Includes unlabelled capsules, proprietary gym blends, internet research chemicals, grey-market powders
categories.generalEffects: Unpredictable biological activity due to variable chemical composition, undeclared adulterants, and zero quality standards.
shortTermRisks: Acute toxic reactions, unexplained allergic anaphylaxis, and organ distress
Sudden loss of consciousness or tachycardia from synthetic analogues
Immediate adverse analytical findings in anti-doping control
longTermRisks: Irreversible renal (kidney) or hepatic (liver) damage from toxic contaminants
Permanent cardiac remodeling and neurological excitotoxicity
Extended competitive athletic bans under the Strict Liability code
signsHelpNeeded: Experiencing tremors, chest pain, or jaundice (yellowing eyes) after starting a new powder
Product packaging missing batch lot numbers, third-party seals, or clear manufacturer details
Seller claims the product is 'for research use only' or 'not for human consumption'
categories.antiDopingRelevance: Carries the highest statistical rate of anti-doping sanctions for inadvertent ingestion of banned SARMs, stimulants, or aromatase inhibitors.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: Immediately cease consumption of unverified batches and bring packaging to a medical toxicologist if symptoms arise.

categories.name: General Drug Awareness
categories.subtitle: Foundational education on clean athletic integrity, peer resilience, and health preservation
categories.generalEffects: Focuses on understanding how substances alter physiology and developing lifelong ethical athletic habits.
shortTermRisks: Falling prey to aggressive commercial marketing or locker-room misinformation
Underestimating the sensitivity of modern anti-doping mass spectrometry
Overlooking the principle of Strict Liability
longTermRisks: Compromising athletic career eligibility through avoidable mistakes
Long-term health damage from unmonitored experimentation
Loss of self-respect, team trust, and clean athletic legacy
signsHelpNeeded: Feeling overwhelming pressure from coaches or teammates to take shortcuts
Experiencing persistent anxiety about athletic performance plateaus
Uncertainty about the legality of everyday medications
categories.antiDopingRelevance: The World Anti-Doping Code requires every athlete to understand their rights and responsibilities under international clean sport guidelines.
categories.professionalSupportGuidance: Connect with certified sports dietitians, sports medicine physicians, and athlete ombudsmen for guidance.

wellnessChecklist.text: Drink adequate water throughout the day (keep urine pale straw-colored)
Eat regular, balanced whole-food meals with adequate protein
Prioritize 7 to 9 hours of uninterrupted restorative sleep
Take a 15-minute gentle walk outdoors in fresh air
Connect with a supportive friend, family member, or mentor
Complete one Play2Protect educational module or puzzle
Avoid high-risk peer environments or unverified supplement offers

healthyEatingGuide.breakfast: Balanced whole-food start: oatmeal or whole-grain toast, 2 eggs or Greek yogurt/tofu, fresh fruit (banana or berries), and a glass of water.
healthyEatingGuide.lunch: Steady afternoon fuel: grilled poultry, fish, or lentils/beans, brown rice or quinoa, mixed steamed or raw vegetables, healthy fats (olive oil or avocado).
healthyEatingGuide.snack: Hydrating energy: a piece of fresh seasonal fruit with a small handful of almonds, or a cup of natural yogurt.
healthyEatingGuide.dinner: Restorative evening meal: lean protein source, roasted sweet potato or whole grains, generous portion of colorful greens, herbal non-caffeinated tea.

dailySupportPlan.action: Watch one verified educational video or complete a short Play2Protect lesson.
Take a short walk, do light mobility stretching, or practice safe light movement.
Reach out to a trusted friend, family member, coach, or supportive peer.
Complete a 1-minute calming breathing exercise or sensory grounding challenge.
Complete a quick Myth vs. Fact or anti-doping puzzle to keep your mind sharp.
Browse verified counsellors and doctors if you need guidance or clinical advice.
